test.title: Planting a hedge instead of a fence

paragraphs.text: A hedge costs more to plant than a wooden fence but lasts far longer. A well-cut hedge of hawthorn may stand for a century, while a fence is usually replaced after fifteen years.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Hedges also shelter birds, and a thick hedge slows the wind across a field better than a solid barrier, which creates gusts on the far side. They must be cut every year or two, usually in late winter.
paragraphs.label: B

document.title: Planting a hedge instead of a fence

items.prompt: A hedge is cheaper to plant than a fence.
A fence normally lasts longer than fifteen years.
A solid barrier causes gusts behind it.
Hawthorn is the best plant for a hedge.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–4. Do the following statements agree with the information in the text? Write TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN.
